newsitem.title: USA: Carter-Wallace's majority stockholder rejects Davis offer.
newsitem.headline: Carter-Wallace's majority stockholder rejects Davis offer.

text.p: Carter-Wallace Inc. said Friday that its biggest shareholder has rejected billionaire investor Marvin Davis' $835 million bid for the maker of Trojan condoms and Arrid deodorant.
Following the news, Carter-Wallace's stock fell $1.625 to $13.875 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Carter-Wallace said that its majority shareholder CPI Development Corp. had informed the company that it has no interest in selling its shares in the proposed transaction.
On Wednesday, Davis Cos. announced that it wanted to buy all the firm's outstanding shares for $18 per share.
Based on Carter-Wallace's 46.39 million shares outstanding, the offer from the financier's Los Angeles-based Davis Cos. was valued at $835 million.
Carter-Wallace said that in light of CPI Development's position, it will not take any further action on Davis' bid.

Most traders had given the buyout deal only a slim chance of succeeding because Carter-Wallace has previously expressed little interest in selling the company. Furthermore, insiders control about 82 percent of Carter-Wallace via common stock and a special class of shares.

Carter-Wallace is dominated by members of the Hoyt family. Chief Executive Officer and Chairman Henry Hoyt Jr. is the son of the executive who took over management of the Carter Medicine Company in 1929. Family members hold other key positions.

Carter-Wallace has long been viewed on Wall Street as an acquisition candidate. At the company's meeting in July, some stockholders criticised its low stock price but a shareholder proposal to consider a merger was rejected.
